verdictText: **APPROVE-WITH-NOTES.** The ledger is exact and re-derivable (admission freeze before any edit; both product leaves byte-identical to the baseline at the red commit and at 27eca6c1; no test byte changed after the red commit; 9 changed files all in the frozen 10-path manifest, plus the reserved admission-review slot = 10 of 15; 36 of 500 counted lines recomputed `--no-renames` from 27eca6c1; only P2CG1F's own lifecycle fields in units.json at each of the three commits; every hash in the three receipts reconciles with the blobs and the author's proof logs; RED reproduced exactly, 5 failed / 73 passed with the receipt's five titles). The behaviour is what the registration and my E carry-forwards asked for: a throwing queue step (confirmApplied included) rejoins once and never rejects the queue; the CF12 close signal is consumed by the existing fixed-prefix match; a bound binding that hears no campaign frame within `APPLICATION_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS` rejoins once, cleared by the first campaign frame, by rejoin and by dispose; a proven discard-flush adoption fences any older guarded refresh by generation, after the version and digest proofs. Both changes are unreachable in production (no shipped creator binds `expectedCampaignId`, so `active` is false and the window is never armed; `loadGeneration` has no reader but the guarded refresh, which only a bound host issues). All 78 registered cases, the Task 14 selector (104), the B (45), C (54), D (119) and E (156) suites, the 35 A1/A2 suites (388) and 82 related suites (675, 2 pre-existing skips) pass on the exact head; typecheck (also at RED), lint (87 warnings / 0 errors), format, both roadmap validators and OpenSpec strict pass; 32 of 32 check runs succeed with names identical to B/C/D/E. The notes are: four of my eight mutants survived, two of them real coverage gaps that matter once receipt mode is live (nothing pins that an offer ends the quiet window, nor that a server heartbeat does not); one latent liveness interaction with G1's planned rebind-on-a-live-transport (a fresh binding re-arms the window on a transport that has already latched); a 60 s-period rejoin cycle against a server that holds the socket open and never sends a campaign frame (bounded, same class as the existing refusal rejoins); and two documentary items for the closure (the behaviour text names neither the quiet window nor the CF14 option chosen). Nothing blocks merge.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes, each with the reviewer's section 5 finding verbatim. None records a product defect. Authority names one pre-existing residual outside CF14 (CF-G6). Privacy records that nothing new reaches the wire. Replay and idempotency record the ordered queue and the once-only rejoin and window. Concurrency records a bounded 60 s rejoin cycle against a silent-but-open server (CF-G4). The two production-relevant coverage gaps are mutants RM-F6 (replay) and RM-F2 (concurrency), carried as CF-G1 and CF-G2. Each verdict field is the closure's reading of the finding, not reviewer text.

authority.verdict: PASS (no defect; one pre-existing residual outside CF14, carried as CF-G6)
authority.finding: **Authority.** The consumer resolves no canonical action and F adds no write: a thrown step and a silent socket both end in `rejoin`, which only flips `live`, clears the window, unsubscribes, closes the transport and signals the hook; the next binding re-reads the authority's baseline from EMPTY. A settle in flight when the binding dies returns before `confirm`, so a dead binding cannot certify an offer it did not finish (pinned: held successor not ACKed; RM-F7 caught). The store change does not alter what is adopted (version and digest proofs unchanged, FM6/RM-F5 caught); it only decides who wins when a proven adoption and an older guarded read interleave, and the proven adoption wins. Residual (CF-G6): the mirror ordering (guarded refresh adopts a newer row first, then an older proven adoption resets the token) is pre-existing, requires a co-op/non-co-op crossing within one GET latency, and ends in the 409 conflict path, not a silent overwrite (`applySavedRecord` writes the token, metadata and cache key, never the live campaign).

privacy.verdict: PASS (no defect; nothing new reaches the wire)
privacy.finding: **Privacy.** Nothing new reaches the wire. The window and the catch send no frame; a rejoin's new `CampaignJoin` carries what E already defined (host: the fold is reset to EMPTY before connecting, so `lastSeq` is -1 and omitted; guest: the mirror's `lastSequence`, which the receipt-mode server ignores). The error text matched on the fixed prefix is never rendered by the consumer. The store serialises nothing new.

replay.verdict: PASS (no defect; the replay-class mutant RM-F6 survived as a coverage gap, carried as CF-G1)
replay.finding: **Replay.** The queue stays ordered: after a throw at step k, steps k+1..n run on the dead binding and neither fold nor ACK (RM-F3 caught). The window fires at most once per binding (cleared and never re-armed), and only one `rejoin` reaches the hook across the timer, the `onError` prefix, the catch and the Error-frame path (pinned: error frame then close -> two connects, not three). The generation is monotonic, so a guarded refresh that captured an older generation can never write later, whichever await it is parked on (both CF14 cases).

idempotency.verdict: PASS (no defect; RM-F1 near-equivalent, timer-count pin offered as CF-G8)
idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** `rejoin` is once-only by `live`; `heard()` is idempotent (`clearTimeout` on a cleared or undefined handle); `dispose` after `rejoin` is a no-op for the timer; a second `rejoin` from the catch after `settle`'s own is a no-op. RM-F1 survived because the leaked handle has no observable effect through `rejoin`'s guard; CF-G8 offers the timer-count pin.

concurrency.verdict: PASS (no defect; bounded 60 s rejoin cycle carried as CF-G4; the concurrency-class mutant RM-F2 survived as a coverage gap, carried as CF-G2)
concurrency.finding: **Concurrency.** `consume` runs synchronously inside the transport's listener dispatch, so `heard()` on the first campaign frame always precedes a timer that could fire in the same tick; the T-1/T boundary is pinned. The chain's catch keeps later steps from waiting on a rejected predecessor. In the store the bump and `applySavedRecord` are one synchronous block, and the guarded refresh's check-and-write pairs are synchronous, so interleaving happens only at await boundaries, each of which re-checks the generation. Liveness judgement: against a server that accepts the socket and sends no campaign frame (the binder's silent `open() === false` return at `bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1252` is such a case), each rejoin arms a fresh window, so the client re-joins once per 60 s indefinitely; bounded (one `CampaignJoin` per T, no tight loop) and in the same class as the pre-existing immediate rejoin on a refusal, but worth a cap or a terminal state when the consumer leaf next opens (CF-G4). Against a legacy server the first legacy baseline ends the window, so there is no 60 s cycle in the G2 period, which is what the author's choice set out to avoid.

quietWindow: **CF-F3, pre-receipt quiet window.** `quiet = active ? setTimeout(rejoin, APPLICATION_CONFIRMATION_TIMEOUT_MS) : undefined` at bind; `heard()` clears it on the first campaign frame (`campaignEventFromMessage(message)` non-null: a CampaignSnapshot or CampaignEvent carrying a valid wire event, offer or legacy), on `rejoin` and on `dispose`. `rejoin` is a hoisted function declaration and the timer fires asynchronously, so the `offError`/`heard` consts it references are initialised by then (no TDZ). Pinned with fake timers: close before receipt mode, no frame -> 1 connect at T-1 ms, 2 at T, no transport signal (`signals: 0`), the new view ACKs `v2-r0`; a legacy baseline frame ends the window (no rejoin over 2T, socket still open); dispose removes exactly one armed timer and nothing fires over 2T. Ruling on the design choice in section 6 item 1.
cf14Fence: **CF14, generation fence.** `adoptFlushedRevision` increments `loadGeneration` after `response.ok`, the `record.version === flushed.baseVersion + 1` proof and the envelope-digest proof, immediately before `applySavedRecord` (one synchronous block). The guarded refresh captures `generation` when it leaves the save chain and re-checks `generation === loadGeneration` at every await boundary in `runLoad` (after the GET, after `json()`, after the staged maxima) and before each write; a bump anywhere before its final `set` returns false with nothing written, and `refreshAfterCommittedCommand`'s re-arm is skipped (`current()` false) because the reconciliation path arms its own save. Unproved flushes (digest or version mismatch) do not bump, so a guarded refresh still completes (pinned x2). `loadGeneration` has exactly three writers (`loadCampaign`, `reset`, now the adoption) and one reader (the guarded refresh), so the bump cannot touch an unguarded load in flight. Ruling on bump-versus-refuse in section 6 item 2.
dormancy: **Dormancy.** Non-test grep at the head: `expectedCampaignId` is set by no shipped caller (only the pass-through in `connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport`); both surface effects connect unbound, so `transport.campaignId` is undefined, `active` is false, no window is armed and `consume` returns before the queue; `installApplicationReceipts` has no caller outside tests; `server.js` is byte-identical. The store bump runs on a non-co-op visibility-return reconciliation in production but has no reader there (guarded refreshes exist only on a bound host). Production behaviour is unchanged.

judgments: **CF-F3 and "any campaign frame" (satisfied).** CF-F3 asked F to own a pre-receipt timeout because E's close signal is silent before receipt mode latches, and not to loop on `socket-closed` without the consumer's say. The implementation covers the gap E left: a bound connection that is closed, hung or never answered before its first offer rejoins once after one confirmation window. Clearing on any campaign frame rather than only on an offer is the right choice today for two reasons. (a) Against a legacy server (the G2 period, when creators bind before H installs the port) the first frame is a legacy baseline; an offer-only clear would rejoin every 60 s against a healthy legacy server, resetting the fold each time. (b) Against a receipt-mode server the binder hydrates a bound, membership-admitted connection exclusively through the application view (`bindCampaignSyncConnection.ts:1244-1249`, `:1276`, `:1412`; `joinMember` is never called when `application` is set), so the first campaign frame it sends is an offer, which latches receipt mode in the transport (`parseServerMessage` sets `receiptIntent` on any `appliedView`) and hands the close signal to E's CF12 from that moment. The window therefore never clears on a frame that leaves the connection unprotected. The dependency on (b) is a server invariant F does not pin; it belongs to the binder's next owner or H (CF-G5). Authority and privacy are untouched: the window only reconnects, and a reconnect sends only the join E already defined. The not-a-loop promise holds per binding; the 60 s cycle against a silent-but-open server is recorded as CF-G4.

**CF14, bump versus refuse (sound; the bump is the better of the two).** CF14 (my P2CF2 wording) offered either the generation bump in `adoptFlushedRevision` or a `migrated.version < get().baseVersion` refusal in the guarded path. The bump is a temporal fence consistent with how `loadCampaign` and `reset` already supersede a guarded refresh, independent of version arithmetic, and it is placed after both proofs, so an unproved adoption disturbs nothing (pinned). It is conservative: it also stops a guarded refresh whose row is newer than the adopted one; the consumer then reports `adjunct-failed`, the transport recovers and the view rejoins from EMPTY, which re-reads everything. That is correct for authority (nothing stale is written) and costs a reconnect in a case that requires a co-op host to race a non-co-op discard flush, which the live campaign's co-op flag makes nearly impossible. The refusal alternative would have let the newer row land but would not have covered a refresh held between its version check and a later await; the bump covers every boundary. The pre-existing mirror race (section 5, authority) is outside CF14's wording and is carried as CF-G6.

**RED shape for the CF-F3 quiet case (acceptable).** The case fails at RED with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'sentRaw')` because `connection.acks(1)` indexes a second socket that the baseline product never creates. The failure is behavioural, not a missing API: the test imports nothing that does not exist at the baseline, it typechecks against the baseline product (section 1 item 4), the TypeError is the direct consequence of the missing rejoin, and the same test's `withinWindow/afterWindow` assertion would have failed as `1 !== 2` had the index been guarded; its companion case ("starts nothing once disposed") fails on a plain `toBe`. The ledger's requirement that RED fail for the behaviour the unit delivers is met. A plain assertion would read better in the log; that is a test-only edit that cannot land post-RED and is carried as CF-G7.

**CF-F6 (lint and cycles).** 87 warnings / 0 errors at the head; the store's max-lines count moved 990 -> 991 (already warned since before F); the consumer does not warn; madge from F's two leaves 1100 files / 173 chains, as the author measured before and after.
**CF-F5 (E-DOC-1).** Closed on main by #2230 (27eca6c1), which F rebased onto; the P2CG1E sentence at the head is main's.

**Carry-forwards directed elsewhere.** CF-F1 and CF-F4 (campaignLaunchAuthorityRoute.test.ts), CF-F2 (campaignSyncTransport.test.ts), CF-F8 (client leaves) and CF-F9 (H) are not F leaves and were correctly not absorbed; they remain with their owners and are restated below only where G1 or G2 owns the leaf.

carryForwards.wording: **CF-G3 (rebind on a live bound transport re-arms the window).** G1 registers the P2CF2 m8 P1 case (host rebind on a live bound transport continuing the lineage). Every `bind` arms a fresh 60 s window regardless of what the transport has already heard; a rebind on a latched, quiet transport (a GM reading the screen for a minute) would therefore close a healthy socket and rejoin from EMPTY, and a real-timer m8 P1 case will not see it. G1 must run its P1 case across one window under fake timers and either prove no spurious rejoin or record the design. A fix, if one is needed, lives in `useCampaignApplicationConsumer.ts` (an F leaf, not G1's): e.g. arm the window only when the transport has not yet delivered a campaign frame, which needs a transport-level or fold-store "heard" marker. Register a successor or an amendment rather than editing an unowned leaf.
